verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's own docs describe faceting as filters that also return distribution data, with aggregated counts per field value. They present this as the basis for e-commerce-style navigation across brand, color, size and price range, with counts shown for each option. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that facet counts for multiple facets come back in the same search response as the results (only implied), detail on how range/numeric facet counts work, and independent hands-on corroboration of faceted navigation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build faceted navigation — filters with live counts across categories, ranges, and attributes — from a single query

citations.quote: Let shoppers narrow products by brand, color, size, and price range while displaying counts for each option.
Faceting returns aggregated counts for field values, powering category navigation in your UI
Facets are filters that also return distribution data. Use them together to build interactive, ecommerce-style navigation.
Filters, ranges, and refinements that turn a long list of results into the right answer.
